commits.summary: Bind nullable application object arrays (verification pending)
commits.body:
The ordinary native property entry constructs bounded arrays whose cells can be null, share any component instance, or hold equal-valued distinct instances. Eligible components are final flat classes with writable int fields and a side-effect-free default constructor. The verifier preserves every field bit and initial identity in its counterexample, interpreter, JVM driver and cache replay. Unsupported component shapes and cross-root graphs have explicit refusals.

The changed suite passed all 7 groups, including 59 Rust test binaries and six Python suites. The new JVM regression recovered four cells with both aliased and distinct objects, non-default fields, and a null cell in a named package. The example 379 validator and test-cost lint passed. A capped probe established the direct mutation equivalence across all initial int values.

The five unchanged reference-cell claims and three independent mutation histories are in job 20261123-114826-qualify-direct-nullable-java-object-arra. Job 20261123-115145-recheck-the-other-55-frozen-native-java remeasures the other 55 original claims. Job 20261123-115155-recheck-the-38-historical-java-statement rechecks the entire historical control set with both strict engines.

commits.summary: Follow public Gson calls through JDK collections (verification pending)
commits.body:
Run Collections.synchronizedMap and ArrayList.addAll from the selected JDK. Replay the virtual toArray callback before taking the receiver state, including mutation, empty results, exceptions and iterator invalidation. A successful bytecode allocation retains its exact runtime class through an interface and a path merge. A library factory with an unknown result still refuses that class observation.

The changed suites passed all seven groups, including 59 Rust test binaries. The selected JDK, native engine and concrete interpreter passed map alias, bulk append and callback exception controls. Example 379 validated with replay. Capped probes established the compatible and exception claims on the original Gson fix. The parent produced a JVM-replayed counterexample at selector 0, and an independent positive property established ClassCastException across all four incompatible calls.

Two initial array qualification jobs stopped because the in-memory scope used tuples while its identical JSON representation used arrays. The replacement compares their serialized forms, with a regression that separately rejects a changed bound. Jobs 20261123-121039-qualify-all-direct-array-heaps-on-the-co and 20261123-121039-qualify-gson-parent-and-fix-and-all-rema recheck all 60 frozen native entries, the changed integrated profiles, and extra direct heap and exact-exception controls. Jobs 20261123-121039-qualify-38-historical-statements-on-the and 20261123-121039-run-both-proof-tier-conformance-tests-af recheck the historical differential and both conformance suites.

commits.summary: Enumerate original Java monitor schedules (verification pending)
commits.body:
A separate two-thread checker follows the frozen caller and worker bytecodes and all completed sequentially consistent instruction interleavings, including the declaring-class monitor of a static synchronized method. It models successful platform-thread construction, start and uninterrupted join. A differential run changes only the treatment of the synchronized modifier. This experiment has its own scope alongside the ordinary verifier's three thread-construction refusals.

The original JVM debugger now also holds the mixed-lock worker before its first instruction until the caller saves its read. All four physical schedules replayed, including both the protected and exposed mixed-lock results. The changed suites passed both groups, the example 391 validator passed with replay, and a capped probe of the mixed case found 239 reachable states and both answers. Job 20261123-122845-enumerate-the-original-two-thread-class collects complete state and schedule counts, instruction-level witnesses, disassembly digests and original JVM observations.
